mo_b_cryptic_wall.blurb: A pale, vertical face of bolted sport climbing on the south side of Robinson Bluff, tucked just beyond the Bee Hive wall along the lower trail. Fifteen routes run roughly 60 to 110 feet, so bring a long rope and a helmet. The grades lean toward the middle of the sport scale: a handful of 5.7s through 5.9s, a solid cluster of 5.10s, and a single 5.11. The dolomite is reddish toward the right end and fades to white heading left, and an obvious left-facing corner starts the right side. It suits climbers stepping up from moderate grades who want tall, sustained pitches. The wall is still being cleaned and developed, so expect some rough spots.

_expect.name: Big and Small Crack Areas "AKA Lefty Wall"

mo_big_and_small_crack_areas_aka_lefty_w.blurb: A compact section at the left end of the Cliff Drive cliffs in Kansas City, set just before the road swings into its sharp bend. A wide crack bounds one side and a left-facing dihedral the other. Fourteen short lines, mostly sport with a pair of trad cracks and one top-rope, all in the 5.6 to 5.8 range, with the bulk at 5.8. That makes it a friendly spot for newer leaders and for learning to place gear in cracks. The limestone is smooth and can feel slick, and vegetation may creep over the wall when it has been left alone.
